transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. Thank you for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm doing this right, I really don't want to take up too much of your time. 

I'm mostly here because... well, people keep acting like I'm just imagining things, and I don't want anyone to think badly of me. I'm a very hard worker, you know, I clean houses for a living. But I know for a fact that the hospital people and some folks from the agency I work for have been watching our house. They even follow my cleaning routes when I'm out working. 

I know they're just doing it to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband, which I am, I promise. I take very good care of him, I'd never neglect him. It's just hard when people don't believe you. Does that... does that make sense why I'd come in to talk to you about it?
When you think about the hospital people and agency folks watching you—do you ever have any doubt that this is actually happening, or are you completely certain it's real?

Oh, um... I really don't want to sound stubborn, Doctor, or like I'm arguing with you. I always try to keep an open mind, I really do. I know how it all sounds, which is why people keep acting like I'm just imagining it. I don't want you to think I'm being difficult. 

But... yes, I am certain it's real. I just know what I see. I know the hospital people and those folks from the agency have been watching our house, and I notice them when I'm out on my cleaning routes. I'm not mad at them for it, really! I know they just want to be absolutely sure I'm taking proper care of my husband, which is a good thing to care about. I just... I wish people wouldn't look at me like I'm making it up when I know it's happening. 

Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not saying the wrong thing. I just want to be honest with you.
How long have you been noticing that the hospital people and agency folks are watching you and your house? Did this start suddenly one day, or did it develop gradually over time?

Well, um... I hope this doesn't make me sound too crazy. I know 11 months sounds like a long time, but that's about how long it's been going on. The feeling that people are watching us, I mean. And... well, I haven't mentioned this yet because I didn't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind, but... I've been hearing voices, too, for about the same amount of time. 

It kind of just started happening. I didn't want to make a big fuss about it, you know? I just kept my head down and kept working. I really hope you don't think less of me for not saying something sooner. I just... I try to handle things on my own so I don't bother anyone. Is that... is that a normal amount of time for something like this to happen? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
When you hear these voices, what are they saying to you? Are they commenting on what you're doing, giving you instructions, or something else?

Oh, um... well, it's usually just one voice. A woman's voice. I really hope you don't think I'm making this up, because it sounds so silly when I say it out loud. 

But even when the house is completely quiet, I'll hear her. Usually she sounds like she's right near the kitchen window. And she's so clear, Doctor, it's just like she's standing right there next to me. She'll tell me things like... like I need to check the locks on the doors, or that I should move my husband's pills to a different spot. 

I know it sounds strange, but I always listen to her, just in case. I mean, it's better to be safe than sorry when it comes to taking care of him, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything perfectly. Does that sound like the sort of thing people usually hear? I really hope I'm not giving you answers that are too weird.

When you hear this woman's voice by the kitchen window, does it sound like it's coming from outside your head, as if someone is actually speaking to you from outside? Or does it feel more like thoughts happening inside your mind?

Oh, um... well, it definitely sounds like it's coming from outside my head. I know I just mentioned she sounds like she's right near the window, but... it really is exactly like that. Like someone is actually standing right there in the room with me. 

Even when the house is completely quiet and I know nobody else is home, I hear her out loud, clear as day. It doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all, it's a real voice speaking to me. I really hope that's an okay answer... I'm trying my best to explain it right so I don't confuse you. Does that make sense, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
If I told you that doctors have examined your house and found no evidence of anyone watching you, what would you think about that? Would it change how you understand what's been happening?

Oh... um. I really don't want to disagree with you, Doctor. I know you're the expert and you're just trying to help, and I hope it doesn't make me seem difficult or... or ungrateful. 

But... well, honestly, that's kind of why I'm here. People keep acting like I'm just imagining it, and it makes me feel so awful, like I'm doing something wrong. But I just... I know the hospital people and some of the folks from the agency have been watching our house. And even on my cleaning routes for work, they've been watching me there, too. I really think they're just checking to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. 

I try so hard to do everything right for him and keep the house perfectly clean, I promise I do. I hope you don't think I'm being stubborn for not just agreeing with the other doctors who checked the house. I just have to be honest with you about what I know is happening. Is it... is it okay that I still feel this way? I really want to be a good patient for you and give you the right answers, I just can't shake the fact that they're checking up on me.

Before these experiences started about 11 months ago, would you say you were functioning completely normally? Like, were you working well, getting along fine with your husband, and not having any concerns about people watching you or hearing voices at all?

Oh, um... well, I really hope I'm remembering this right, because I don't want to give you the wrong timeline or make things confusing. But... it actually hasn't been just 11 months. I hope it's okay to correct you, Doctor, I know you have so many patients to keep track of. 

It's been a little bit longer than that. I think this whole change really started about a year and two months ago... right after my husband was in the hospital for his heart. Before that... yes, I think I was doing okay. I was working my cleaning routes and everything was just normal, quiet. No voices or worrying about people checking up on me. It was only after he came home from the hospital that things started to feel... different. 

I just wanted to make sure you had the exact right time frame, so you can do your job properly. I hope that's helpful? I'm really trying to be as accurate as I can for you.

I appreciate you correcting me on the timeline. Let me ask you something important: Looking back now, do you think there's any possibility at all that what you're experiencing—the voices and the feeling of being watched—might not be real, even if you're not sure? Or do you feel completely certain that it's all definitely happening exactly as you perceive it?

Oh... um, I really wish I could say maybe it isn't real. I know that's probably what you want to hear, and I really want to give you the answer that makes you happy. I hate feeling like I'm being difficult or... or like I'm not cooperating with you. I promise I'm not trying to be stubborn. 

But... well, like I mentioned before, that's exactly why I came in to get help. People keep acting like I'm just imagining the whole thing, and it makes me feel terrible, like I'm doing something wrong or letting my husband down. But I just... I know it's real. I know the hospital people and the folks from the agency are watching our house, and they're watching me on my cleaning routes, too. They just want to make sure I'm taking proper care of him. 

I'm so sorry if that's the wrong answer, Doctor. I really am. I just have to be honest with you because I know you can't help me if I'm not truthful. Do you... do you understand why I feel so certain about it? I hope you're not upset with me for saying that.

When you think about everything that's been happening—the watching, the voices, the concerns about your husband—have you ever had even a moment where you wondered if maybe your mind might be playing tricks on you, or has it always felt absolutely certain and real to you with no doubt whatsoever?

Oh, um... I feel like I'm just repeating myself, and I really hope you don't think I'm being difficult. I know you just asked me this, and I want so badly to give you a different answer, one that makes sense to you medically. I really do. 

But... well, no, I haven't ever thought my mind was playing tricks on me. That's actually the whole reason I'm here seeking help. Everyone around me keeps acting like I'm just imagining it all, and it's so upsetting because it makes me feel like I'm doing something wrong. But I just know it's happening. I know the hospital people and the agency folks are watching the house, and checking on me when I'm doing my cleaning routes. They just want to make sure I'm doing a good job taking care of my husband. 

I'm sorry, I know that's exactly what I just said a minute ago. I hope you aren't frustrated with me for not being able to see it another way. I'm just trying to be completely honest with you so you can help me. Is that... is that alright?

In the past year or so, have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep but still felt rested, or felt like your thoughts were racing much faster than normal? Or a time when you were much more active or talkative than you usually are?

Oh, well... I don't want you to think I'm acting out of control or doing anything bad. I really try my best to just be productive and helpful. But... I suppose there are times when I do have a whole lot of energy. I hope it's okay that I just use it to get things done? 

Like, I'll get moving way before daylight... just cleaning the house, cooking, calling about appointments, and making new lists to keep everything organized. I even take on extra church errands on top of my regular cleaning routes. Everyone around me keeps telling me I need to slow down, but I just feel fine and ready to go, so I don't really see the harm in it. 

I'm really just trying to be a good wife and a hard worker... I hope you don't think that means something is wrong with me? I just want to make sure everything is taken care of properly. Did I answer that right for you, Doctor?

When you're up before daylight doing all those activities, do you actually need less sleep than usual—like feeling completely rested after only a few hours of sleep—or are you just waking up early and then staying busy all day?

Oh, um... well, I hope it doesn't sound like I'm doing something wrong, because I really just use the time to be productive. But... yes, I suppose I don't really need much sleep when I get like that. 

Many nights I'll only sleep maybe two or three hours, and then I just wake up feeling completely ready to go. I'll get right up and start scrubbing the floors or sorting through all our paperwork. And the funny thing is, I'm not even tired like I used to be when I had a short night's sleep. I just feel perfectly rested and ready to work. 

I know it probably sounds a little strange, but I really do just try to use that extra time to make sure the house is perfectly clean and my husband has everything he needs. I hope you don't think that's a bad thing? I'm just trying to be helpful and do my best... is it okay that I feel that rested on so little sleep?

During those times when you're sleeping only a few hours but feeling completely rested and full of energy—would you say your mood felt especially good, happy, or elevated compared to your normal mood? Or did you just feel energized but your mood stayed about the same as usual?

Oh, um... well, I don't want to make it sound like I'm overly happy or acting silly or anything like that. I really just try to stay focused on my work and my responsibilities. 

I wouldn't say I feel unusually happy or... or elevated, like you said. I just feel very awake and ready to get things done. My mood is just... well, it's just me, you know? Just me, but with enough energy to finally catch up on all the chores and make sure everything is perfect for my husband. 

I'm just a normal, hardworking person during those times, just trying to be useful. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want you to think I'm acting inappropriately or anything. Does that make sense to you, Doctor?
